# Decisions: branch-visibility

- 2026-09-21T10:22:20.145Z — rule: **Never write to, or rewrite, another checkout's copy of a record; reading across copies is read-side only and adds no event type.** — chose **`sofar list` and `sofar status` fold the UNION of every copy of a log by default. The copies are this checkout's file, every other worktree's working file (uncommitted appends included, read as files with no subprocess), and every local branch NOT merged into HEAD and not checked out anywhere, read at its tip through one `git cat-file --batch`. Duplicate ids are dropped and this checkout's lines stay first, so their line numbers and warnings are unchanged. Output names where the extra events live and what this checkout alone holds. It renders nothing extra, byte-identical to before, when no other copy adds an event. `--here` restores the single-copy view. Remote-tracking refs are opt-in with `--remotes` (operator said "do it" without ruling on remotes, so the conservative default stands).** over (a) Remote-tracking refs on by default. (b) Reading every branch, merged ones included. (c) Moving the record off-branch, or writing events through to main's copy (rejected in note 01M31PRW). (d) Leaving the default local and adding the union as an opt-in flag. because Measured 2026-09-21: memory-lead's copies hold 11, 143, 132 and 149 of 158 events, so any single copy misreports. The fold is ulid-ordered and convergent (SPEC §Cursor primitive (sync-ready contract)), so the union is exactly what merging every branch would give. (b) costs nothing in correctness to skip: logs are append-only and merge=union, so a branch merged into HEAD has its whole committed log already in HEAD's. That is 4 unmerged refs here, not 13. (a) pulls in abandoned remote branches, and a remote branch that matters usually also exists locally. (d) keeps the misreport as the default, which is the reported bug.
